div.p: Daily Yield looks beyond the headline to the money questions that matter to you. Real questions, careful research and clear next steps — with the arithmetic in the open.
Is your savings account really earning?
Illustration. Real return = 1.0294 ÷ 1.051 − 1. Rates are assumptions, not live quotes.
The $5,000 card at 24% APR
Illustration on a $5,000 balance. Minimums are designed to keep you paying, not to clear the debt.
What does a 10-year delay cost?
Long-run world-equity average, before inflation. The money is identical — only the start date moves.
What does a 1% fee quietly take?
Illustration, annual compounding. Fees eat the gains and the original money, every single year.
Prices double faster than you think
The rule of 72 — the five-second mental sum every household should own.
The subscription you forgot
Open your app store and bank statement twice a year. Silent debits are the modern leak.
The emergency fund, in numbers
Illustration. Boring, liquid, untouched — an emergency fund is sleep, not strategy.
The classic split. Percentages scale with any income, any currency, any country.
Avalanche vs snowball on $14,000
From our 13,996-household simulation. Maths prefers avalanche; humans sometimes need snowball.
One extra EMI a year on a 20-yr loan
Illustration. One extra instalment a year quietly amputates years of interest.
$200 a month for 30 years
Illustration, monthly compounding. Time in the market is the whole trick.
The daily $4 coffee, invested
Not a war on coffee — a price tag on habits, so you choose them deliberately.
Your 10% raise vs 6% inflation
Always subtract inflation from any raise. Nominal numbers flatter everyone.
The tax-free head start
Illustration at 30% marginal tax. ISA, 401(k), EPF, super — every country has one. Use it.
Your credit score is real money
Lenders price your discipline. Utilisation is the fastest lever you control.
Gold vs equities, 50 years
Illustrative long-run figures, before taxes. Nobody knows the next 50 years — diversify anyway.
Pay yourself first
Save what remains and there is never anything left. Reverse the order; the rest adapts.

Net worth: the only scoreboard
Assets minus liabilities, tracked quarterly. One number tells the truth about the direction.
Small leaks, big ships
Illustration at 7%. Leaks look tiny monthly and enormous annually — audit both ways.

section.p: Daily Yield is Kushal K. Daga's public desk, informed by his work as a Certified Accountant: real arithmetic instead of opinion, country and date stamped on every figure, and plain language for the decisions that stay with you — a first salary, a home loan, a retirement plan. Nothing to sell you; nothing stored about you.
